newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Norilsk says no output stoppages.
newsitem.headline: Russian Norilsk says no output stoppages.

text.p: Russian Norilsk Nickel's flagship plant had no output disruptions on Thursday as a deadline set by workers for a salary arrears deal arrived, a company spokesman said on Thursday.

"The most important thing is that the x-hour has come, and there is no information that would say that protests, strikes or work stoppages are taking place," RAO Norilsky Nickel spokesman Sergei Vetchinin said.
He said that some management and labour representatives were meeting in the Arctic town of Norilsk, where the plant, the Norilsk mining and metallurgical complex, is based.
He declined to provide specifics on what kind of arrangements had been made with workers, saying only, "We can state that the conflict is being decided in a civilised way."
Interfax news agency had said on Monday that a reconciliation commission grouping both sides had agreed a repayment schedule for salary arrears, which total 1.3 trillion roubles.
Vetchinin said the commission had signed a protocol outlining how potential labour disputes in future would be resolved.
The Norilsk group is a major producer of nickel, copper, platinum, palladium and other metals.
